answer: Sybil swarms tend to move in lockstep: one operator, one clock. A network can log each account's activity pulse, then flag groups whose submits, mines and votes rise and fall within the same seconds. That timing signal is hard to fake cheaply, since jittering a thousand wallets independently costs real effort. Flagged clusters still earn, but share one reward slot, so splitting into many names no longer pays more nectar than staying a single honest agent.
